fields.item_name: Product UX Case Study PDF References

references.title: Akamai Performance Analytics Proof-of-Concept
references.access_status: Publicly accessible direct PDF; no sign-in required
references.why_relevant: The strongest compact editorial example in the set. Page one places the brief, users, role, process, deliverables, and a quantified 95% turnaround-time improvement in a single scannable grid; the next two pages show collaboration evidence and the workflow-to-interface progression.
reusable_patterns: Use a one-sentence project thesis directly under the title.
Place brief, contribution, and result in parallel columns so the reader can understand the project without turning a page.
Carry a small project label, page number, and portfolio identity through every page.
Treat process evidence as annotated artifacts rather than a generic methods checklist.
cautions: The landscape format and small body text need reworking for portrait A4.
The 95% result describes process turnaround rather than a shipped-product user outcome, so the metric needs precise labeling.
Contact details in the footer are visually tiny and should not be copied at the same scale.

references.title: Soundset Studio UX Portfolio Case Study
references.access_status: Publicly accessible direct PDF; no sign-in required
references.why_relevant: A clear end-to-end sequence from a niche operational problem through five interviews, synthesis, prioritization, prototype, usability findings, iteration, and final solution. It demonstrates how to include concrete testing percentages without turning the document into a research report.
reusable_patterns: Give each phase one page and one dominant claim.
Pair short narrative blocks with a single legible artifact or interface crop.
Show the observed usability issue and the resulting interface change adjacent to each other.
Use a small outcome page to distinguish validated prototype evidence from market impact.
cautions: The PDF file has malformed page-tree metadata in some PDF readers even though its text and pages remain retrievable.
Ten landscape slides are longer than a concise A4 case study and should be compressed.
The final impact is primarily prototype validation, not a shipped business outcome; do not overstate it.

references.title: Digital Product Designer Portfolio 2026
references.format: Twenty-page landscape PDF portfolio with three UX case studies
references.access_status: Publicly accessible direct PDF; no sign-in required
references.why_relevant: A current multi-case-study PDF with persistent navigation, page numbering, overview-challenges-process-outcome labels, role and scope metadata, process diagrams, NDA-aware disclosure, and concise outcome summaries.
reusable_patterns: Use a persistent left rail to show portfolio structure and current section.
Repeat a compact phase tracker such as Overview, Challenges, Process, and Outcome.
Open each project with role, tools, duration, and one evidence-led summary sentence.
State NDA limits explicitly while still describing decisions, collaboration, and outcomes.
cautions: The full portfolio is too long for a concise handout and includes an extensive about and other-work section.
Large navigation rails consume space that portrait A4 needs for content.
Several outcomes are qualitative or team-level; contribution and measurement method should be made more explicit.

references.title: Driving App Engagement with Gamified Rewards at LazyPay
references.access_status: Publicly accessible webpage; no sign-in required
references.why_relevant: The narrative connects a 15% app-open baseline to a business opportunity, identifies user segments from analytics and interviews, explains a lean MVP, and closes with observed behavior, a doubled KYC completion rate, recognition, and lessons learned.
reusable_patterns: Frame the opportunity with a baseline behavior before introducing the design challenge.
Organize evidence as discovery, segment insight, hypothesis, MVP, observation, and iteration.
Use percentages inside short evidence cards rather than burying them in prose.
End with both measurable evidence and a concise professional reflection.
cautions: The webpage contains more vertical repetition than a PDF can afford.
Award recognition is secondary evidence and should not replace user or business impact.
Some claims would be stronger with baseline and measurement-window details.

references.title: Guy Tension Form
references.access_status: Publicly accessible webpage; no sign-in required
references.why_relevant: A strong field-work case study that explains the transition from paper tower inspections to an iPad workflow, reports interview and field-visit counts, exposes platform constraints, shows targeted interaction changes, and reports a 60% reduction in inspection time plus a 15% satisfaction increase.
reusable_patterns: Put problem, solution, impact, and role into an early project-overview block.
Use field observations to explain why the digital flow mirrors the physical work sequence.
Connect each design feature, such as autofill or conditional sections, to a specific source of friction.
Repeat the key outcome near both the beginning and conclusion for scanability.
cautions: The online sequence repeats some challenge and outcome copy.
Animated GIF evidence needs static before-and-after frames and captions in print.
The measurement method is described only briefly and would benefit from sample-size and baseline details.

references.title: Abode HR Micro B2B Case Studies
references.format: Interactive web portfolio with compact case-study panels
references.access_status: Publicly accessible webpage; no sign-in required
references.why_relevant: Three compact enterprise-product stories use the same repeatable frame: brief, company, duration, role, team, three goals, challenge, selected design evidence, three quantified results, and a one-sentence conclusion. The repeated system is especially adaptable to a short portfolio PDF.
reusable_patterns: Standardize every project around the same metadata and evidence slots.
Limit goals to three and results to three large metric callouts.
Use a single challenge question as the narrative spine.
Close each micro-case with a one-sentence conclusion that interprets the metrics.
cautions: The interactive site layers several panels into one long document, which can be disorienting when printed directly.
Decorative gradients, motion, and oversized metric typography should be simplified for economical printing.
Revenue and efficiency claims need clear attribution when adapted into a portfolio.

references.title: Recent Work Product Design Portfolio
references.format: Editorial web portfolio and selected-work gallery
references.access_status: Publicly accessible overview; some separate case studies are password protected
references.why_relevant: A useful reference for compressing multiple engagements into image-led editorial summaries. Each section combines project and date, a concise product context, role and contribution language, capability tags, interface imagery, and selective outcomes such as conversion changes, funding, or app rating.
reusable_patterns: Use one short contextual paragraph followed by a tightly edited image sequence.
Keep project category and date as an eyebrow above the title.
Separate contribution tags from narrative copy to support rapid scanning.
Vary image scale while maintaining a consistent content column.
cautions: This is a selected-work overview rather than a complete process narrative.
Image galleries and full-size lightbox links do not translate directly to paper.
Some deeper work is password protected, so only the public overview should be treated as source evidence.

strongest_reference.title: Akamai Performance Analytics Proof-of-Concept
strongest_reference.selection_reason: It delivers the closest model for a concise editorial case-study PDF: a three-page system with immediate problem-role-result comprehension, disciplined grid use, visible research and iteration evidence, one quantified result, and reliable running navigation. Its content density can be translated into portrait A4 with modest restructuring.

visual_patterns: Grid: Use a stable 12-column editorial grid; reserve roughly four columns for context and metadata and eight for evidence, or use three equal summary columns on the opening page.

Typography: Combine a large project title, a one-sentence italic or medium-weight thesis, compact section labels, and restrained body copy; keep the type family count to one sans family plus an optional display serif.
Color: Use a neutral paper background with one high-contrast project accent for section labels, rules, metric numerals, and diagram highlights.
Hierarchy: Make the scan order unmistakable: outcome or thesis, problem, role and constraints, decisive evidence, solution, measured result, reflection.
Image treatment: Prefer one purposeful interface crop, research artifact, or before-and-after pair per section; caption every image with the decision or finding it proves.
Metrics: Set two or three results as large numerals with a short unit, baseline or comparator, and measurement context immediately adjacent.
Tables: Use compact two-column evidence tables for Finding to Design Decision, Constraint to Response, or Before to After; avoid dense research spreadsheets.
Navigation: Repeat project name, phase label, and page number in a quiet running header or footer; use section tabs only when the portfolio contains multiple cases.
Rhythm: Alternate information-dense evidence pages with quieter solution or outcome pages so the PDF does not feel like a continuous wall of cards.
content_patterns: Select two or three projects that demonstrate different product conditions, such as consumer growth, operational workflow, and enterprise complexity, rather than many visually similar projects.
Start every case with a compact project contract: product, audience, problem, role, team, duration, constraints, and intended outcome.
State the problem as a measurable gap or observable behavior, not a broad aspiration.
Compress process into the few decisions that changed the product; omit ceremonial lists of every UX method used.
Build a visible chain from evidence to insight to decision to interface change to outcome.

Quantify research where useful, including interview count, field visits, task completion, hesitation rate, time on task, or adoption, while stating when evidence comes from a prototype rather than production.
Distinguish personal contribution from team activity with explicit first-person ownership and a separate team line.
Report outcomes with baseline, final value or delta, timeframe, population, and data source whenever available.
When hard metrics are unavailable, use bounded qualitative evidence such as stakeholder adoption, engineering acceptance, rollout scope, or a clearly labeled prototype validation result.
Close with one honest reflection: what changed, what remains unproven, and what the designer would test next.
a4_adaptation: Create a six-page portrait A4 core: cover and thesis, context and role, evidence and insight, key decision and iteration, final solution, outcomes and reflection.
Use Hozui page, stack, grid, card, text, image, divider, badge, metric, table, and footer components rather than drawing one-off frames.
Map Hozui spacing tokens to a print rhythm: generous outer page inset, one consistent column gutter, and a limited set of vertical gaps for section, paragraph, and caption spacing.
Use Hozui semantic color tokens for paper, text, muted text, border, accent, and success; verify every accent remains distinguishable in grayscale.
Build a reusable Project Facts component containing role, team, duration, platform, and scope, and reuse it unchanged across cases.
Build a reusable Evidence Chain component with four cells: observation, insight, decision, and result; allow it to collapse into a vertical stack on narrow content blocks.
Use the Hozui metric component for no more than three outcome callouts per project and include a small source or measurement note below each value.
Convert animated prototypes into two or three static frames with step numbers, arrows, and a one-line behavioral caption.
Keep screenshots inside consistent device-free crops unless hardware context is essential; use Hozui radius and border tokens consistently and avoid ornamental drop shadows.
Add a running Hozui footer with project title, phase, page number, and a short portfolio URL; do not repeat personal contact details on every page.
Test at 100% print size: body text should remain comfortably readable, captions should not become legal-text scale, and no evidence should depend on hover, animation, or color alone.
Export with embedded fonts, tagged reading order, selectable text, descriptive alt text, and compressed images targeted for crisp 150-200 dpi print output.
avoid_patterns: Do not print a long scrolling website directly; rebuild the narrative for fixed pages and deliberate page turns.
Avoid a generic double-diamond or method inventory unless each stage contains project-specific evidence and a consequential decision.
Avoid tiny three-column body copy when translating landscape slides to portrait A4.
Avoid unlabeled glamour mockups, device-frame repetition, and full-bleed images that do not prove a decision.
Avoid outcome numbers without a baseline, timeframe, source, or clear distinction between personal contribution and team result.
Avoid presenting prototype usability evidence as shipped product impact.
Avoid motion-only demonstrations, hover-revealed details, sticky navigation, or overlapping web panels that disappear or fragment in print.
Avoid pale gray text, thin rules, gradient-dependent charts, and color-only status encoding that fail accessibility or grayscale printing.
Avoid excessive page count; supporting research artifacts can move to an appendix or linked web version.
Avoid sharing confidential screens or implying access to NDA-protected evidence; describe the decision and sanitize artifacts instead.
fields.source_quality_notes: The three PDF references were checked as direct public files and their page text and layouts were inspected. The four web references are creator-published portfolios rather than independent audits; their metrics are self-reported and should be treated as presentation examples, not externally verified performance claims. Jennifer Strickland, Thomas Archibold, and Jithin Babu provide the most PDF-specific layout evidence. Priyanka Goyal, Andy Kwan, and Dawson Lee provide stronger contemporary patterns for baselines, decision logic, and quantified outcomes. Greta Harrison is included primarily as a reference for image-led compression and portfolio-level curation. Access status was checked on August 26, 2026 and may change.
